body:
This PR replaces #35, adding an extensive set of CPU/GPU compilation tests and fixing several issues they uncovered:
- `Core.kwcall` needs its recursion limit disabled to support nested `reduce`/`accumulate` calls with the `init` keyword argument, as explained in [this comment](https://github.com/CliMA/UnrolledUtilities.jl/pull/35#issuecomment-5289065049)
- `unrolled_push` needs to be generated using `ntuple` instead of splatting to avoid the `max_tuple_splat` limit from `base/compiler/types.jl`
- `unrolled_applyat` needs to call `Base.throw_boundserror` instead of `throw(BoundsError(...))` to make use of the `@device_override` in `CUDA.jl`
- `unrolled_allunique` needs to perform a reduction instead of using `unrolled_unique` to avoid the runtime comparison limit of `unrolled_unique`
- `unrolled_accumulate` for `StaticBitVector` had a syntax error introduced in an earlier PR

Several tests are still marked as broken:
- `unrolled_any`/`unrolled_all`/`unrolled_count` can be unstable on GPUs when given functions of non-singleton values that return runtime booleans
- `unrolled_applyat`/`unrolled_findmax`/`unrolled_findmin`/`unrolled_flatmap` can also be unstable on GPUs with non-boolean runtime values

Each of these issues could be resolved in one of three ways: fix a bug in the text harness, fix an inefficiency in the source code, or identify a new compilation limit and add a corresponding `@testset` to `compilation_limits.jl`.

After the lingering issues are fixed in a future PR, these tests can be generalized to a user-friendly analogue of `@test_opt` from `JET.jl`, and we can use them throughout other packages. Unlike `@test_opt`, these tests precisely target what we need on every device — CPUs must be able to run without heap allocations, and GPUs must be able to compile kernels without IR errors.

In addition, this PR moves the temporary patches from ClimaCore's `Utilities.Unrolled` module into UnrolledUtilities:
- New `unrolled_setindex`/`unrolled_insert` functions, which are analogous to `Base.setindex` and `insert!`
- A fast path for `Tuple` arguments in `unrolled_map`, which reduces latency and allocations during compilation
- A `@propagate_inbounds` version of `unrolled_map`, which allows it to support indexing operations; this is combined with the new fast path methods to avoid defining another function
title: Add tests for CPU/GPU compilation limits
